Article 209-2  (1) If the property that should be confiscated pursuant to the provisions of Article 198-2, paragraph (1) or Article 200-2 (hereinafter referred to as "illegal property" in this Article, paragraph (1) of the following Article, and Article 209-4, paragraph (1)) is mixed with property other than illegal property, and that illegal property is to be confiscated, the portion of the property generated by the mixing (referred to as "mixed property" in the following paragraph and paragraph (1) of the following Article) which corresponds to the amount or quantity of the illegal property (limited to the portion related to the mixing) may be confiscated.
(2) The provisions of the preceding paragraph also apply if a third party with knowledge of the circumstances acquires the mixed property (limited to mixed property in which illegal property related to the provisions of Article 200-2 is mixed).
(Requirements for Confiscation)
Article 209-3  (1) Confiscation under the provisions of Article 198-2, paragraph (2) is limited to the case in which the illegal property or the mixed property does not belong to any person other than the perpetrator; provided, however, that if a person other than the perpetrator acquires the illegal property or the mixed property by coming to know the circumstances of the crime after the crime has been committed (excluding the case in which property that has been provided as performance of legal obligation has been received or the case in which property that has been provided as performance of obligation related to a contract (limited to a contract under which the creditor is to provide a considerable amount of economic benefit) that has been concluded without knowing that obligations under the contract are to be performed by illegal property or mixed property, at the time of concluding the contract), the illegal property or mixed property may be confiscated even when the property belongs to a person other than the perpetrator.
(2) If property on which a superficies right, a mortgage, or any other right exists is to be confiscated pursuant to the provisions of Article 198-2, paragraph (1) or Article 200-2, and a person other than the perpetrator has acquired the right before the crime or a person other than the perpetrator acquires the right after the crime without knowledge of the circumstances, the right is to be kept in existence.
Chapter VIII-2 Special Provisions on Procedures Concerning Confiscation
(Procedures for Confiscation of the Property of a Third Party)
Article 209-4  (1) If a claim, etc. that is illegal property (meaning property other than real property and movables; the same applies in paragraph (1) of the following Article and Article 209-7) belongs to a person other than the accused (hereinafter referred to as a "third party" in this Article), and the third party is not allowed to participate in the proceedings of the case under public prosecution, a judicial decision for confiscation may not be made.
(2) The provisions of the preceding paragraph also apply when property on which a superficies right, a mortgage or any other right of a third party exists is sought to be confiscated pursuant to the provisions of Article 198-2, paragraph (1) or Article 200-2, and the third party is not allowed to participate in the proceedings of the case under public prosecution.
(3) If property on which a superficies right, a mortgage or any other right of a third party exists is to be confiscated, and the right is to be kept in existence pursuant to the provisions of paragraph (2) of the preceding Article, the court must pronounce to that effect simultaneously with the rendering of confiscation.
(4) If a judicial decision for confiscation without the pronouncement referred to in the preceding paragraph becomes final and binding with regard to a right that is to be kept in existence pursuant to the provisions of paragraph (2) of the preceding Article, a person that holds the relevant right and was unable to claim the right in the proceedings of the case under public prosecution due to a reason unattributable to that person may, demand a judicial decision to the effect that the case falls under a case in which the right should be kept in existence.
(5) If the judicial decision referred to in the preceding paragraph is made, compensation is made pursuant to the rules applicable to the compensation for confiscated property that has been disposed of specified in the Criminal Compensation Act (Act No. 1 of 1950).
(6) With regard to the procedures concerning confiscation of property provided for in paragraphs (1) and (2), unless otherwise provided for in this Act, the provisions of the Act on Emergency Measures on Criminal Procedure to Confiscate Items Owned by Third Parties (Act No. 138 of 1963) apply mutatis mutandis.
(Disposition of Confiscated Claims)
Article 209-5  (1) A claim, etc. that has been confiscated with regard to the crime referred to in Article 197, paragraph (1), item (v) or (vi) or paragraph (2), Article 197-2, item (xiii), or Article 200, item (xiv) must be disposed of by a public prosecutor.
(2) If a judicial decision for confiscation of a claim that should be confiscated with regard to the crime referred to in Article 197, paragraph (1), item (v) or (vi) or paragraph (2), Article 197-2, item (xiii), or Article 200, item (xiv) becomes final and binding, a public prosecutor must notify the debtor of the claim to that effect by sending an extract of the written judgment of the judicial decision for confiscation.
(Registration Based on a Judicial Decision for Confiscation)
Article 209-6  In the case of commissioning a related organization to make registration of transfer of right based on a judicial decision for confiscation of property for which transfer of right requires registration with regard to the crime referred to in Article 197, paragraph (1), item (v) or (vi) or paragraph (2), Article 197-2, item (xiii), or Article 200, item (xiv), if there is a registration related to restriction on a disposition that has ceased to be effective as a result of the confiscation or a registration related to acquisition of right that has been extinguished as a result of the confiscation, or if there is a registration related to a preservation order for confiscation or a collateral preservation order under the provisions of Chapter IV, Section 1 of the Act on Punishment of Organized Crimes and Control of Crime Proceeds (Act No. 136 of 1999), a deletion of the registration must also be commissioned.
(Special Provisions on Criminal Compensation)
Article 209-7  With regard to the details of compensation under the Criminal Compensation Act for execution of compensation of a claim, etc. to be confiscated with regard to the crime referred to in Article 197, paragraph (1), item (v) or (vi) or paragraph (2), Article 197-2, item (xiii), or Article 200, item (xiv), the provisions of Article 4, paragraph (6) of that Act apply mutatis mutandis.
Chapter IX Investigations in Criminal Cases
(Questioning, Examination, and Retention)
Article 210  (1) An official of the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (hereinafter referred to as the "Commission" in this Chapter) (hereinafter such an official is referred to as a "Commission official" in this Chapter) may request a suspect or witness in a criminal case (meaning a crime referred to in Chapter VIII, which is specified by Cabinet Order as a crime that is detrimental to the fairness of purchase and sale of securities or other transactions of securities, or derivatives transactions, etc.; hereinafter the same applies in this Chapter) (hereinafter such a suspect or witness is referred to as a "suspect or witness in a criminal case" in this paragraph and paragraph (1) of the following Article) to appear, ask questions to a suspect or witness in a criminal case, inspect articles in the possession of or abandoned by a suspect or witness in a criminal case, or retain articles that a suspect or witness in a criminal case voluntarily submits or abandons, if this is necessary for investigating a criminal case.
(2) The Commission official may inquire with public agencies, or public or private organizations, and request them to report necessary particulars for the investigation of criminal cases.
(Inspection, Search, or Seizure)
Article 211  (1) If it is necessary for investigating a criminal case, a Commission official may conduct an inspection; search the body of a suspect or witness in a criminal case, an object of a suspect or witness in a criminal case, or a residence or any other place associated with a suspect or witness in a criminal case; seize an article of evidence or a thing the official considers to be an object that should be confiscated; or conduct a seizure with an order to produce a copy of records (meaning ordering the keeper of an electronic or magnetic record or a person with the authority to access an electronic or magnetic record to copy the necessary electronic or magnetic record onto a recording medium, or print out that record, and seizing that recording medium; hereinafter the same applies in this Chapter) through a warrant issued in advance by the judge of the district court or summary court that has jurisdiction over the locality of the Commission; provided, however, that a Commission official may search the body of a witness, an object associated with a witness, or a residence or any other place associated with a witness only if there are sufficient circumstances for the official to discern the existence of an object to be seized.
(2) If an object to be seized is a computer, starting from a recording medium connected via telecommunication lines to that computer which may be reasonably supposed that is used to store an electronic or magnetic record that has been made or altered using that computer or an electronic or magnetic record that may be altered or erased using that computer, the computer or the other recording medium may be seized after the electronic or magnetic record is copied onto that computer or that other recording medium.
(3) In the cases referred to in the preceding two paragraphs, in cases of urgency, a Commission official may make a disposition referred to in the preceding two paragraphs with a warrant issued in advance by the judge of the district court or the summary court that has jurisdiction over the locality of the person who is to record or print out the object or place to be inspected, the body, object, or place to be searched, the object to be seized, or the electronic or magnetic record.
(4) In requesting a warrant referred to in paragraph (1) or the preceding paragraph (hereinafter referred to as a "warrant" in this Chapter, excluding Article 222-3, paragraphs (4) and (5)), a Commission official must submit materials that confirm the existence of a criminal case.
(5) If a request under the preceding paragraph is made, the judge of the district court or the summary court must deliver a warrant to a Commission official which states the name of the suspect in the criminal case (for a corporation, the name of the corporation), the charged offense, the object or place to be inspected, the person, object, or place to be searched, the object to be seized, or the electronic or magnetic record to be recorded or printed out and the person who is to record or print out the record, and the government position and name of the requester, the valid period, the fact that after the valid period ends, the warrant may not be executed and must be returned, the date of issuance and the name of the court, and bears their name and seal.
(6) In the case referred to in paragraph (2), in addition to the particulars prescribed in the preceding paragraph, the warrant must state the scope of the recording medium that is connected via telecommunication lines to the computer to be seized, and whose electronic or magnetic records are to be copied.
(7) A Commission official may deliver a warrant to another Commission official and have that official execute the inspection, search, seizure, or seizure with an order to produce a copy of records.
(Seizure from a Person That Handles Communications)
Article 211-2  (1) If it is necessary for investigating a criminal case, a Commission official may seize a document concerning a postal item, correspondence item, or telegraphic communication sent by or addressed to a suspect in a criminal case, which, based on the provisions of laws and regulations, is stored by or in the possession of a person handling communications, by receiving delivery of a warrant.
(2) A Commission official may seize a document concerning a postal item, correspondence item, or telegraphic communication not falling under the preceding paragraph, which, based on the provisions of laws and regulations, is stored by or in the possession of a person handling communications only if there are sufficient circumstances to suppose that the document is related to a criminal case.
(3) Upon making the disposition under the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs, Commission official must notify the sender or recipient to that effect; provided, however, that this does not apply if notifying the sender or recipient is likely to hinder the investigation of the criminal case.
(Request for Preservation of Electronic or Magnetic Records of Communications History)
Article 211-3  (1) If it is necessary for carrying out the seizure or the seizure with an order to produce a copy of records, a Commission official may specify the necessary electronic or magnetic records from among the electronic or magnetic records of the sender, recipient, date and time, and other communications history, for telecommunications that are recorded in the course of business, and request in writing that a person engaged in the business of making equipment to be used for telecommunication available for other persons' communications or a person that has established equipment which is used for telecommunication and that is capable of intermediating the communications of unspecified or many persons for their own business not to erase the specified electronic or magnetic records during a fixed period of no longer than 30 days. In such a case, if the Commission official comes to find that it is no longer necessary to carry out the seizure or the seizure with an order to produce a copy of records concerning those electronic or magnetic records, the Commission official must withdraw that request.
(2) If it is particularly necessary, the period during which the request is made not to erase the records pursuant to the provisions of the preceding paragraph may be extended by a period of no longer than 30 days; provided however, that the period during which the request is made not to erase the records may not exceed 60 days in total.
(3) If it is necessary to do so in making a request under the provisions of paragraph (1), the Commission official may request that the particulars of that request not be divulged without reason.
(Dispositions in Lieu of the Seizure of a Recording Medium Containing Electronic or Magnetic Records)
Article 211-4  If the object to be seized is a recording medium containing electronic or magnetic records, a Commission official may make any of the following dispositions in lieu of the seizure of the recording medium:
(i) copying, printing out, or transferring the electronic or magnetic records contained in the recording medium to be seized onto another recording medium, and then seizing that other recording medium; or
(ii) having the person subject to the seizure copy, print out, or transfer the electronic or magnetic records contained in the recording medium to be seized onto another recording medium, and then seizing that other recording medium.
(Restriction on the Execution of Inspection, Search, or Seizure at Night)
Article 212  (1) It is prohibited for an inspection, a search, a seizure, or a seizure with an order to produce a copy of records to be made during the period between sunset and sunrise unless the warrant indicates that this may be executed at night.
(2) An inspection, a search, a seizure, or a seizure with an order to produce a copy of records that was initiated before sunset may be continued after sunset, if this is found to be necessary.
(Presentation of a Warrant)
Article 213  The warrant for an inspection, a search, a seizure, or a seizure with an order to produce a copy of records must be presented to the person subject to those dispositions.
(Proof of Identity)
Article 214  When carrying out questioning, examination, retention, inspection, search, seizure, or seizure with an order to produce a copy of records pursuant to the provisions of this Chapter, a Commission official must carry an identification card and present it if requested by a person concerned.
(Necessary Dispositions at the Time of Inspection, Search, or Seizure)
Article 215  (1) If it is necessary to do so in order to carry out an inspection, a search, qa seizure, or a seizure with an order to produce a copy of records, a Commission official may release a lock, open a seal, or make other necessary dispositions.
(2) The dispositions referred to in the preceding paragraph may also be made with respect to retained objects, seized objects, or objects seized with an order to produce a copy of records.
(Request for Cooperation from the Person Subject to the Disposition)
Article 215-2  If the object to be inspected or the object to be seized is a recording medium containing electronic or magnetic records, a Commission official may ask the person subject to the inspection, search, or seizure to operate the computer or provide other necessary cooperation.
(Prohibiting Entrance and Exit During Dispositions)
Article 216  While carrying out questioning, examination, retention, inspection, search, seizure, or seizure with an order to produce a copy of records pursuant to the provisions of this Chapter, a Commission official may prohibit any person from entering or exiting the place without permission.
(Attendance of the Person in Charge)
Article 217  (1) When carrying out an inspection, a search, a seizure, or a seizure with an order to produce a copy of records at a person's residence, or at a mansion, building, or other place that a person watches over, a Commission official must have the owner or manager (or a representative, agent, or other person that may act on the owner's or manager's behalf) or the employee or co-habiting adult relative of the owner or manager, present at the site.
(2) In the case referred to in the preceding paragraph, if it is not possible to have any of the persons prescribed in that paragraph present at the site, a Commission official must have an adult neighbor of the person, or another police officer or official of the local government, present at the site.
(3) When searching a female, a Commission official must have an adult female present; provided, however, that this does not apply in cases of urgency.
(Assistance of Police Officers)
Article 218  A Commission official may request the assistance of police officers if this is necessary at the time the Commission official carries out an inspection, a search, a seizure, or a seizure with an order to produce a copy of records.
(Preparation of a Record)
Article 219  (1) Upon carrying out questioning pursuant to the provisions of this Chapter, a Commission official must prepare a record of the questioning, have the person the official questioned inspect the record, or read it aloud to the person, ask the person whether it contains any errors, and if the person makes a proposal for an addition to, deletion from, or alteration of the record, enter the person's statement in the record, and sign and seal it, as well as have the person sign and seal it; provided, however, that if the person that was questioned will not or cannot sign and seal the record, it is sufficient to append a note of this.
(2) Upon carrying out an examination or retention pursuant to the provisions of this Chapter, a Commission official must prepare a record of this, and sign and seal the record.
(3) Upon carrying out questioning, examination, retention, inspection, search, seizure, or seizure with an order to produce a copy of records pursuant to the provisions of this Chapter, a Commission official must prepare a record of this, show the recod to a person that was present, and sign and seal it, as well as have that person sign and seal it; provided, however, that if the person that was present will not or cannot sign and seal the record, it is sufficient to append a note of this.
(Preparation of a Retention Inventory)
Article 220  Upon carrying out a retention, seizure, or seizure with an order to produce a copy of records, a Commission official must prepare an inventory and deliver a certified copy of this to the owner, possessor, or keeper of the retained object, seized object, or object seized with an order to produce a copy of records (including a person rendered a disposition under the provisions of Article 211-4) or to any other person that may act on their behalf.
(Handling of Retained Objects)
Article 221  A Commission official may collect a storage certificate and have the owner or possessor of a retained object, seized object, or object seized with an order to produce a copy of records that is inconvenient to transport or store, or any other person that the Commission official finds to be appropriate, store that object, with the consent of the person in question.
(Return of Retained Objects)
Article 222  (1) If it becomes unnecessary to keep a retained object, seized object, or object seized with an order to produce a copy of records, a Commission official must return it to the person to whom it should be returned.
(2) If the Commission is unable to return a retained object, seized object, or object seized with an order to produce a copy of records referred to in the preceding paragraph because the address or residence of the person to whom it should be returned is unknown or for any other such reason, the Commission must issue public notice of this.
(3) If no request is filed for the return of the retained object, seized object, or object seized with an order to produce a copy of records to which the public notice under the provisions of the preceding paragraph concerns after six months have elapsed since the day of the public notice, the object vests in the national treasury.
(Delivery of a Recording Medium Seized after Transfer)
Article 222-2  (1) If it becomes unnecessary to keep a recording medium that was seized after transferring or having a person transfer electronic or magnetic records pursuant to the provisions of Article 211-4, and the person subject to the seizure is a different person from the owner, possessor, or keeper of the recording medium, a Commission official must deliver the recording medium to the person subject to the seizure or allow the person to copy the electronic or magnetic records.
(2) The provisions of paragraph (2) of the preceding Article apply mutatis mutandis to delivery or copying under the provisions of the preceding paragraph.
(3) If no request is filed for the delivery or copying under the provisions of paragraph (1) after six months have elapsed since the day of the public notice under the provisions of paragraph (2) of the preceding Article as applied mutatis mutandis pursuant to the preceding paragraph, the Commission official is not required to make the delivery or have the person make the copying.
(Request for Expert Opinion)
Article 222-3  (1) If it is necessary for investigating a criminal case, a Commission official may commission a person with relevant expertise to present an expert opinion or commission that person to perform interpretation or translation services, with regard to a retained object, seized object, or object seized with an order to produce a copy of records.
(2) A person that has received a request for an expert opinion under the provisions of the preceding paragraph (referred to as an "expert" in paragraphs (4) and (5)) may destroy the object for which an expert opinion was requested, with the permission of the judge of the district court or summary court that has jurisdiction over the locality of the Commission.
(3) A request for the permission referred to in the preceding paragraph must come from a commission official.
(4) If the request referred to in the preceding paragraph has been filed and the judge finds the request to be reasonable, the judge must issue a warrant to a Commission official which states the name of the suspect in the criminal case, the charged offense, and the object to be destroyed; states the name of the expert; states the government position and name of the requester; states the valid period; indicates that after the valid period ends, the warrant may not be executed and must be returned; states the date of issuance and the name of the court; and bears the judge's name and seal.
(5) An expert must show the warrant referred to in the preceding paragraph to a person subject to the disposition referred to in paragraph (2).
(Report to the Commission)
Article 223  Upon completing an investigation of a criminal case, a Commission official must report the results of the investigation to the Commission.
(Investigation of a Criminal Case by a Finance Bureau Official)
Article 224  (1) With the approval of the Commission, the Director-General of a Local Finance Bureau or the Director-General of a Local Finance Branch Bureau is to designate persons who will be in charge of investigations of criminal cases from among the officials of a Local Finance Bureau or a Local Finance Branch Bureau.
(2) A person designated by the Director-General of a Local Finance Bureau or the Director-General of a Local Finance Branch Bureau pursuant to the provisions of the preceding paragraph (hereinafter referred to as the "official of a Local Finance Bureau, etc." in this Chapter) is deemed to be a Commission official, and the provisions of Article 210 through the preceding Article apply. In such a case, the term "of the Commission" in Article 211, paragraph (1) is deemed to be replaced with "of the Local Finance Bureau or Local Finance Branch Bureau to which the official belongs", the term "Commission" in Article 222, paragraph (2) is deemed to be replaced with "the Director-General of a Local Finance Bureau or the Director-General of a Local Finance Branch Bureau", the term "Commission" in Article 222-3, paragraph (2) is deemed to be replaced with "the Local Finance Bureau or the Local Finance Branch Bureau to which the official of a Local Finance Bureau, etc. prescribed in Article 224, paragraph (2) who is deemed to be a Commission official referred to in the preceding paragraph pursuant to the provisions of Article 224, paragraph (2) belongs", and the term "to the Commission" in the preceding Article is deemed to be replaced with "to the Director-General of a Local Finance Bureau or the Director-General of a Local Finance Branch Bureau".
(3) If the Director-General of a Local Finance Bureau or the Director-General of a Local Finance Branch Bureau receives a report from the official of a Local Finance Bureau, etc. under the provisions of the preceding Article as applied pursuant to the preceding paragraph following the deemed replacement of terms, the Director-General must report the content of the report to the Commission.
(4) The Commission guides and supervises the Director-General of a Local Finance Bureau or the Director-General of a Local Finance Branch Bureau in the investigation of a criminal case.
(5) The Commission may directly guide and supervise the official of a Local Finance Bureau, etc., if it finds this to be necessary in connection with the investigation of a criminal case.
(Execution of Duties Outside the Jurisdictional District)
Article 225  The official of a Local Finance Bureau, etc. may execute duties outside the jurisdictional district of the Local Finance Bureau or Local Finance Branch Bureau to which the official belongs, if it is necessary for the official to do so in order to investigate a criminal case.
(Accusation by the Commission)
Article 226  (1) If the Commission is convinced that a criminal offense has taken place based on the investigation of a criminal case, it must file an accusation and if there are any retained objects, seized objects, or objects seized with an order to produce a copy of records, it must hand over the objects together with the retention inventory, seizure inventory, or inventory of seizure with an order to produce a copy of records.
(2) If a retained object, seized object, or object seized with an order to produce a copy of records referred to in the preceding paragraph is related to the storage under the provisions of Article 221, the Commission must use the storage certificate referred to in that Article to keep it in custody, as well as notify the keeper referred to in that Article to that effect.
(3) If a retained object, seized object, or object seized with an order to produce a copy of records is handed over pursuant to the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs, the object is deemed to have been seized pursuant to the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Act No. 131 of 1948).
(Special Provisions on Specially Permitted Services for the Transitional Period)
Article 3-3  (1) Notwithstanding the provisions of Article 29 and Article 58-2, a person other than a financial instruments business operator, a financial institution prescribed in Article 33, paragraph (1), a notifier of specially permitted services, and a notifier of specially permitted services for foreign investors, etc. who engages in investment management business (meaning the investment management business prescribed in Article 28, paragraph (4); hereinafter the same applies in this Article) in a foreign country based on foreign laws and regulations (hereinafter referred to as a "foreign investment management business operator" in this Article) may engage in specially permitted services for the transitional period" by notifying the Prime Minister of the following particulars in advance pursuant to the provisions of Cabinet Office Order; provided, however, that this does not apply if a period of five years that starts on the date of notification (if the person has become a financial instruments business operator, etc. (limited to one that conducts investment management business), a notifier of specially permitted services, or a notifier of specially permitted services for foreign investors, etc. during the five-year period, at the time when the person has become the financial instruments business operator, etc., the notifier of specially permitted services, or the notifier of specially permitted services for foreign investors, etc.), or if the person comes to fall under Article 63-10, paragraph (3), item (ii) as applied pursuant to the provisions of paragraph (4).
(i) the person's trade name or name;
(ii) the amount of stated capital or total amount of contributions, if it is a corporation;
(iii) the names of its officers, if it is a corporation (including the domestic representative, if it is a foreign corporation);
(iv) if the person has an employee specified by Cabinet Order, the name of that employee;
(v) the type of business (meaning the type of business related to the acts set forth in the items of paragraph (5));
(vi) the name and location of the person's principal business office or office (if it is a foreign corporation, including the principal business office or office in Japan);
(vii) the name and location of the business office or office for performing specially permitted services for the transitional period;
(viii) if the person is engaged in other business, the type of that business; and
(ix) other particulars specified by Cabinet Office Order.
(2) The notification under the provisions of the preceding paragraph must be made by the day on which a period of five years have elapsed starts to run from the day on which the Act Partially Amending the Banking Act and Other Acts for Ensuring Reinforcement and Stability of Financial Functions in Response to Socioeconomic Changes due to the Impact of the COVID-19 Infection (Act No. 46 of 2021) comes into effect.
(3) Notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph (1), a person that falls under any of the following items must not perform specially permitted services for the transitional period:
(i) a person falling under any of the following sub-items:
(a) a person that has not obtained the registration of the same kind as the registration referred to in Article 29 (including permission or any other administrative disposition similar to such a registration) for conducting investment management business in a foreign country (limited to a foreign country specified by Cabinet Office Order as a country or region that has a system concerning persons engaging in investment management business that is found to be at a level equivalent to that of Japan in protecting investors; the same applies in (b) of this item, (d) of the following item, and paragraph (5), item (i)) pursuant to the provisions of laws and regulations of that foreign country;
(b) a person for whom the period specified by Cabinet Order that starts to run from the time investment management business has been commenced in a foreign country based on foreign laws and regulations has not passed (excluding a person falling under a case specified by Cabinet Order);
(c) a person that falls under any of Article 29-4, paragraph (1), item (i), (a) through (c);
(d) a person specified by Cabinet Office Order as a person that does not have a sufficient personnel structure to perform specially permitted services for the transitional period in an appropriate manner;
(e) a person specified by Cabinet Office Order as a person that is found not to have in place the necessary system for performing specially permitted services for the transitional period in an appropriate manner; or
(f) a person mainly engaged in investing property subject to investment (meaning money and other property invested by that person on behalf of a right holder prescribed in Article 42, paragraph (1)) as an investment in securities set forth in Article 2, paragraph (1), item (ix) and other securities specified by Cabinet Order;
(ii) if the person is a corporation, a person that falls under any of the following sub-items:
(a) a person that falls under Article 29-4, paragraph (1), item (ii);
(b) a person that does not have a business office or office in Japan;
(c) a foreign corporation that has not designated a domestic representative;
(d) a foreign corporation that has not been given the assurance referred to in Article 189, paragraph (2), item (i) by the foreign regulatory authority for financial instruments prescribed in paragraph (1) of that Article in a foreign country where its principal business office or office, or its business office or office for performing investment management business is located;
(e) a person that has a person falling under Article 29-4, paragraph (1), item (v), (d) 1. or 2. among their major shareholders that is an individual (meaning the major shareholders prescribed in paragraph (2) of that Article; if the corporation is a subsidiary company of a holding company (meaning the subsidiary company prescribed in paragraph (4) of that Article; the same applies in paragraph (7), including the major shareholders of the holding company; the same applies in (f)); or
(f) a person that has a person falling under one of Article 29-4, paragraph (1), item (v), (e) 1. through 3. among their major shareholders that are corporations; or
(iii) if the person is an individual, a person that falls under any of the following sub-items:
(a) a person that falls under Article 29-4, paragraph (1), item (iii); or
(b) a person that has an address in a foreign country.
(4) If a foreign investment management business operator is to perform specially permitted services for the transitional period pursuant to the provisions of paragraph (1), the notification under the provisions of that paragraph is deemed to be the notification under the provisions of Article 63-9, paragraph (1) and the specially permitted services for the transitional period are deemed to be specially permitted services for foreign investors, etc. prescribed in Article 63-8, paragraph (1), and the provisions of this Act (excluding Article 29-4, paragraph (1), item (i), (b), 7. and item (ii), (f), 7., Article 63-9, paragraphs (1) and (6), and Article 63-11), the Residential Basic Book Act (Act No. 81 of 1967), the Act on the Provision of Financial Services, and the Act on Prevention of Transfer of Criminal Proceeds (Act No. 22 of 2007) (including the provisions of orders based on these provisions). In such a case, the term "paragraph (6), item (i)" in Article 63-9, paragraph (2), items (i) and (ii) is deemed to be replaced with "Article 3-3, paragraph (3), item (i) of the Supplementary Provisions"; in Article 63-9, paragraph (8), the term "Article 39" is deemed to be replaced with "Article 38-2, Article 39" and the term "Article 42-7" is deemed to be replaced with "Article 42-7, Article 42-8"; in Article 63-9, paragraph (9), the phrase "If the right set forth in Article 2, paragraph (2), item (v) or (vi) connected with an act set forth in paragraph (1), item (i) of the preceding Article which a notifier of specially permitted services for foreign investors, etc. has commenced as specially permitted services for foreign investors, etc. no longer falls under the category of the right prescribed in paragraph (1), item (i) of the preceding Article" is deemed to be replaced with "If the discretionary investment contract connected with an act set forth in Article 3-3, paragraph (5), item (i), (a) of the Supplementary Provisions which a notifier of specially permitted services for foreign investors, etc. has commenced as specially permitted services for the transitional period no longer falls under the discretionary investment contract prescribed in sub-item (a) of that item, the right indicated on the beneficiary securities of a foreign investment trust which is connected with the act set forth in sub-item (b) of that item no longer falls under the right indicated on the beneficiary securities of a foreign investment trust prescribed in sub-item (b) of that item, or the right set forth in Article 2, paragraph (2), item (vi) connected with an act set forth in Article 3-3, paragraph (5), item (i), (c) of the Supplementary Provisions no longer falls under the right prescribed in Article 3-3, paragraph (5), item (i), (c) of the Supplementary Provisions" and the phrase "or the money invested or contributed by foreign investors, etc. (meaning the foreign investors, etc. prescribed in paragraph (2) of the preceding Article) that hold that right no longer falls under money that has been mostly invested or contributed by non-residents" is deemed to be deleted; the term "law or regulation or" in Article 63-13, paragraph (2), item (i) is deemed to be replaced with "law or regulation (including a foreign law or regulation) or"; the phrase "items of Article 63-8, paragraph (1)" in Article 194-7, paragraph (2), item (ii)-3 is deemed to be replaced with "items of Article 3-3, paragraph (5) of the Supplementary Provisions"; and any other necessary technical replacement of terms is specified by Cabinet Order.
(5) The term "specially permitted services for the transitional period" as used in paragraph (1) and the preceding two paragraphs means the performance of any of the following acts on a regular basis by a foreign investment management business operator at its business office or office established in Japan:
(i) the following acts connected with the investment management business conducted in a foreign country based on foreign laws and regulations:
(a) the act set forth in Article 2, paragraph (8), item (xii) performed based on a discretionary investment contract (limited to those concluded only with foreign investors, etc. (limited to those that do not fall under any of the following persons)) (excluding acts specified by Cabinet Office Order as those likely to compromise the protection of investors):
1. a special purpose company (meaning a special purpose company as defined in Article 2, paragraph (3) of the Act on Securitization of Assets) that issues asset backed securities (meaning asset backed securities as defined in Article 2, paragraph (11) of that Act) which have been acquired by persons other than foreign investors, etc.;
2. a business operator or a person seeking to become a business operator in a silent partnership agreement (meaning a silent partnership agreement provided for in Article 535 of the Commercial Code) that concerns an investment business for the rights set forth in Article 2, paragraph (2), item (v) or (vi), which has persons other than foreign investors, etc. as silent partners; and
3. a person that is specified by Cabinet Office Order as being equivalent to a person set forth in 1. or 2.;
(b) the act set forth in Article 2, paragraph (8), item (xiv), which is to invest money contributed by a foreign investor, etc. that holds rights indicated on the beneficiary certificates of a foreign investment trust prescribed in paragraph (1), item (x) of that Article (limited to rights held only by foreign investors, etc. (limited to those that do not fall under any of sub-item (a) 1. through 3.; hereinafter the same applies in this paragraph)) (excluding acts specified by Cabinet Office Order as those likely to compromise the protection of investors);
(c) the act set forth in Article 2, paragraph (8), item (xv), which is to invest money (including things specified by Cabinet Order as being similar to money) that has been invested or contributed by a foreign investor, etc. that holds rights set forth in Article 2, paragraph (2), item (vi) (limited to rights related to the same business subject to investment (meaning an business subject to investment provided for in item (v) of that paragraph) in which foreign investors, etc. are the only holders of those rights (excluding the acts specified by Cabinet Office Order as those likely to compromise the protection of investors); or
(ii) the following acts connected with the acts set forth in the preceding item:
(a) the handling of public offering or handling of private placement related to beneficiary certificates of a foreign investment trust prescribed in Article 2, paragraph (1), item (x), foreign investment securities prescribed in item (xi) of that paragraph, or rights set forth in paragraph (2), item (vi) of that Article, which is carried out with foreign investors, etc. in connection with an act set forth in (a) of the preceding item performed by a person (limited to handling of public offering or handling of private placement specified by Cabinet Order as having little likelihood of persons that are not foreign investors, etc. to acquire those securities and excluding handling specified by Cabinet Office Order as that likely to compromise the protection of investors);
(b) the public offering or private placement of beneficiary certificates of a foreign investment trust prescribed in Article 2, paragraph (1), item (x), which is carried out with foreign investors, etc. in connection with an act set forth in (b) of the preceding item performed by a person (limited to public offering or private placement specified by Cabinet Order as having little likelihood of allowing persons that are not foreign investors, etc. to acquire the beneficiary certificates and excluding offering or placement specified by Cabinet Office Order as that likely to compromise the protection of investors); and
(c) the public offering or private placement of rights set forth in Article 2, paragraph (2), item (vi), which is carried out with foreign investors, etc. in connection with an act set forth in (c) of the preceding item performed by a person (limited to public offering or private placement specified by Cabinet Order as having little likelihood of allowing persons that are not foreign investors, etc. to acquire the rights and excluding those specified by Cabinet Office Order as being likely to compromise the protection of investors).
(6) The term "foreign investor, etc." as used in the preceding paragraph means one of the following persons:
(i) a foreign corporation or an individual that has an address in a foreign country;
(ii) in addition to the persons set forth in the preceding item, a person specified by Cabinet Order as being closely related to a foreign investment management business operator; and
(iii) a person that is specified by Cabinet Office Order as a person equivalent to the persons set forth in the preceding two items.
(7) The provisions of paragraph (1), paragraph (2), paragraph (3) (excluding item (i), (a) and (b) and item (iii)), and paragraph (4) apply mutatis mutandis if a subsidiary company of a foreign investment management business operator (excluding one that falls under paragraph (3), item (i) or (ii) (excluding (b) and (c))) performs the act set forth in Article 2, paragraph (8), item (xii) (excluding acts specified by Cabinet Office Order as those likely to compromise the protection of investors) on a regular basis based on a discretionary investment contract (limited to a contract concluded only with the foreign investment management business operator) at their business office or office established in Japan. In such a case, the phrase "specially permitted services for the transitional period" in those provisions is deemed to be replaced with "services connected with the acts prescribed in paragraph (7)"; the phrase "the type of business related to the acts set forth in the items of paragraph (5)" in paragraph (1), item (v) is deemed to be replaced with "services connected with the acts prescribed in paragraph (7)"; the term "that paragraph" in paragraph (4) is deemed to be replaced with "paragraph (1)"; and any other necessary technical replacement of terms is specified by Cabinet Order.
